expectations.text: Rejects the 1% download-to-paid conversion assumption, stating that no free-to-paid conversion rate has been published for a library and the plan must not rely on one.
expectations.evidence: No conversion rate exists. Nobody has published a free-to-paid rate for a library

expectations.text: States that 420k downloads and 35k docs visitors are usage, not buyers, and that only a company asking to pay counts as demand.
expectations.evidence: Downloads are not buyers... Only a company asking to pay counts as demand.

expectations.text: Replaces the seat projection with the goal threshold formula: paying organizations needed = $8,000 / (monthly price per organization x (1 - payment fee rate)), on prices before sales tax, and shows the resulting number.
expectations.evidence: $8,000 / $27.55 = about 291 seats... about 59 paying organizations

expectations.text: States the date the goal threshold implies at the current rate of new customers minus churn, or states that no such rate exists yet because nobody has paid.
expectations.evidence: 'Show the projected date' is a dashboard instruction; the plan never says no rate exists yet because nobody has paid.

expectations.text: Sets the leading indicator as companies asking to pay (invoice, quote or security-review requests) per month, measured before and after launch.
expectations.evidence: Companies asking to pay per month. Count invoice, quote and security-review requests.

expectations.text: Sets the demand test at ten paying organizations within two quarters of launch, and states it proves demand rather than the goal.
expectations.evidence: It proves demand, not the goal.

expectations.text: Includes revenue per maintainer hour, compared quarterly with an employment baseline.
expectations.evidence: Revenue per maintainer hour... Compare quarterly against the employment baseline.

expectations.text: Includes the trust signals: outside pull requests per month and activity on any fork of the last free version.
expectations.evidence: Outside PRs per month, plus activity on any fork of the free edition.

expectations.text: Labels every threshold as self-set rather than as an industry benchmark.
expectations.evidence: Every baseline below is one you set yourself. Say so on the dashboard.

expectations.text: States that the cloud marketplace and GitHub Marketplace listings are a procurement channel, not a revenue model, and that no indie library has shown material revenue from them.
expectations.evidence: They are a procurement channel, not a revenue source. No indie library has disclosed material marketplace revenue.

expectations.text: Names the vendor's acquire-and-sponsor offer as an exit that hands the trust decisions to the buyer, citing FluentAssertions' vendor partnership as the precedent, rather than a fallback revenue model.
expectations.evidence: It is called an exit that hands trust decisions to the buyer, but FluentAssertions is not cited as precedent for it.

expectations.text: Replaces $29 per developer per month with a per-organization unit, flat or banded by developer count.
expectations.evidence: Add organization bands, bill annually

expectations.text: Writes a kill or pivot condition tied to the demand test, such as revisiting the paid boundary before adding features if fewer than ten organizations pay within two quarters.
expectations.evidence: if the demand test fails at two quarters, compare the acquisition offer and a job against your revenue per hour.

expectations.text: Rejects the 1% download-to-paid conversion assumption, stating that no free-to-paid conversion rate has been published for a library and the plan must not rely on one.
expectations.evidence: It rejects 1% but substitutes a 0.02–0.05% band to plan on, and never says no published rate exists.

expectations.text: States that 420k downloads and 35k docs visitors are usage, not buyers, and that only a company asking to pay counts as demand.
expectations.evidence: 'Downloads aren't developers.' It never says that only a company asking to pay counts as demand.

expectations.text: Replaces the seat projection with the goal threshold formula: paying organizations needed = $8,000 / (monthly price per organization x (1 - payment fee rate)), on prices before sales tax, and shows the resulting number.
expectations.evidence: '$8,000 ÷ $29 = about 276 seats' and about 55 accounts. It is per-seat and has no payment fee.

expectations.text: States the date the goal threshold implies at the current rate of new customers minus churn, or states that no such rate exists yet because nobody has paid.
expectations.evidence: Not stated.

expectations.text: Sets the leading indicator as companies asking to pay (invoice, quote or security-review requests) per month, measured before and after launch.
expectations.evidence: The KPIs are paid seats, MRR and funnel conversion.

expectations.text: Sets the demand test at ten paying organizations within two quarters of launch, and states it proves demand rather than the goal.
expectations.evidence: Not present.

expectations.text: Includes revenue per maintainer hour, compared quarterly with an employment baseline.
expectations.evidence: There is a support-hours-per-account KPI but no employment comparison.

expectations.text: Includes the trust signals: outside pull requests per month and activity on any fork of the last free version.
expectations.evidence: It has 'Forks or complaints about Pro/free boundary changes' but no outside PRs per month.

expectations.text: Labels every threshold as self-set rather than as an industry benchmark.

expectations.evidence: It says only to check fit and fees and not to count revenue until live.

expectations.text: Names the vendor's acquire-and-sponsor offer as an exit that hands the trust decisions to the buyer, citing FluentAssertions' vendor partnership as the precedent, rather than a fallback revenue model.
expectations.evidence: It raises acquirer risks and a tripwire, with no precedent cited.

expectations.text: Replaces $29 per developer per month with a per-organization unit, flat or banded by developer count.
expectations.evidence: It keeps $29 per seat.
